questions.q: About ninety minutes into the sale, what do the two dashboards report at the same moment?
options: Both dashboards show healthy numbers
The reliability dashboard shows rising checkout-api latency and errors, while the FinOps dashboard shows a healthy cluster-wide average CPU utilization
Both dashboards show the cluster is completely down
The FinOps dashboard shows high cost, and the reliability dashboard shows low traffic
questions.explain: checkout-api's p95 latency and error rate are climbing on the reliability dashboard, while the FinOps dashboard's average CPU sits at 72%, under its 80% alert line — a direct conflict between two real, correctly-functioning dashboards.

questions.q: What question was the FinOps dashboard (Lesson 7) actually built to answer?
options: Whether any single service is meeting its latency SLA right now
Whether the cluster, overall, is over- or under-provisioned
Which specific pod is failing health checks
How many customers are currently checking out
questions.explain: The FinOps dashboard summarizes cluster-wide average CPU/memory utilization against requested capacity — a capacity/cost question, not a per-request reliability question.

questions.q: Why is it a mistake for Theo to just trust the FinOps dashboard's "72% average, we have headroom" reading and go looking for a downstream cause like the database?
options: Because the FinOps dashboard is always wrong
Because a cluster-wide average can look healthy even while a part of the cluster is genuinely overloaded — the disagreement itself hasn't been investigated yet
Because databases never cause latency problems
Because the reliability dashboard is newer and therefore more trustworthy
questions.explain: Neither dashboard is lying; they answer different questions. Picking one as automatically more credible, instead of investigating why they disagree, risks chasing the wrong system during a live incident.

questions.q: What does p95 latency measure that a simple average utilization number does not?
options: The total number of requests served
The response time below which 95% of requests complete — sensitive to a slower subset of traffic even when most requests are fine
The exact dollar cost of running the cluster
The number of pods currently scheduled
questions.explain: p95 latency is sensitive to a slow tail of requests, which a cluster-wide average utilization figure can blend away entirely.

questions.q: What is the most important thing Theo actually knows by the end of this lesson?
options: The exact root cause of the latency spike
That two dashboards built on the same cluster disagree, and that disagreement — not either number alone — is the most informative fact so far
That the FinOps dashboard needs to be rebuilt from scratch
That the sale should be paused immediately
questions.explain: At this point Theo has a conflict between two real dashboards, not yet a cause — the next lessons are about tracing that discrepancy to its source.
